title: Recorded pending tasks at run stop
contract: New runs snapshot the live pending queue at stop, including run status and last recorded candidate reason. Full bound logs reconcile pending IDs with the summary. Results investigation provides a pending-at-stop filter, linked snapshot records and readable task details. Earlier snapshots can precede later confirmed outcomes; contradictory later snapshots are flagged. Repeated exports retain stable event IDs.
limitations: Last candidate reasons do not diagnose every robot. Missing reasons remain explicit, and old logs without snapshots retain unknown outcomes. Cancelled, geometric-stop, filtered and reduced logs do not establish full-run coverage. Snapshots explain queue state, not global feasibility or task completion.

title: Free corridor endpoint trim and extension
contract: Select one explicit corridor and a free corridor-node endpoint, then choose/pick a same-floor boundary corridor. Preview moves the endpoint along its source line to the boundary interior and joins the boundary by subdivision using that existing node identity. Source directed distance overrides scale by the new/old geometric length; boundary overrides divide proportionally. Other attributes, door restrictions and supported route/resource references are retained. Apply is one undoable transaction. Independent simulator case changes a disconnected route into 16 m / 8 s travel with one-way and door restrictions retained.
limitations: Junction/location/lift relocation, endpoint merging, automatic corridors, parallel or behind-anchor intersections and existing occupied intersections are rejected. Only the chosen boundary is joined; other crossings are unchanged. This is graph editing, not swept-footprint clearance validation or general CAD trimming.

title: Project model layers and current drawing layer
contract: Versioned project-owned layers control visibility and undoable editing locks. Assignment, rename and move-contents removal preserve graph objects. Locked corridors protect endpoint positions and reciprocal records. Hidden objects leave canvas selection before redraw. New locations, nodes and corridors use the current visible unlocked layer; copying and subdivision inherit source layers. Archive storage and undo retain layer state. Default remains available. Optional theme/custom colour, five patterns and 0.5-6 screen-pixel widths style corridors and location outlines; selection and route overlays retain their own styles. Styles persist and are undoable.
limitations: Editor locks are not protection against external file edits. Node-symbol styling, per-object overrides, plot/export styles, a combined drawing/model manager and human acceptance remain open. Custom colours require suitable contrast for the chosen theme. Hidden topology still participates in model-aware drawing snaps. Layers do not alter routing permissions or simulation geometry.

title: Optional supply at depleted pickup locations
contract: Default false. Reuse unreserved eligible stock first; supply unique unnamed objects at physical pickup only. Record addition events and population counts.
limitations: Exact identities, same-container returns, staged recovery and reserved empty-bin exchanges still require stock. Ordinary outbound creation unchanged. Exported events require verbose evidence. Counts do not prove a globally minimum population.

title: Explicit unverified direct fallback for local inventory-bay manoeuvres
contract: Default off. When enabled, local bay invalid_endpoint and search_exhausted failures with finite endpoints use direct movement with existing speed/alignment timing. The fallback is never stored in the validated waypoint cache. Forward and reversed segments carry local_manoeuvre_validation=unverified_direct_fallback and the original failure reason; full movement event details preserve these values. Project checks warn when the option is enabled. Playback uses the original robot body and heading display without the added reference cross.
limitations: This is an explicit modelling override, not validated collision-free geometry. It does not bypass malformed coordinates, graph restrictions, traffic failures or unsupported detailed-mode features. Per-movement audit requires full event records; reduced legacy logs may lack movement detail.

title: Drawing reuse, responsive graph input and selected-object deletion
contract: Undo/redo preserves unchanged drawing inputs and PDF page rasters. Unchanged DXF scene items survive graph redraws. Graph tools bypass native underlay hover dispatch; PDF alignment keeps native interaction. Drag redraws are coalesced on a 16 ms timer and release flushes final position and panels. Canvas Delete, Edit Delete selected and right-click Delete selected share an atomic undoable selection operation, preserving existing department/lift deletion rules. Text-field Delete does not delete graph objects. Demand generation is accessible under Configuration in the sidebar.
limitations: Graph geometry is still redrawn during movement; the timer is not a frame-rate guarantee. The recorded synthetic DXF benchmark measures scene refresh, not end-to-end LTN performance. Changing DXF mappings still loads the required drawings. Reference cleanup follows existing model deletion rules; Project checks remain necessary after structural edits.

title: Workbench startup and portable project lifecycle
contract: The unified amr_app.py entry point opens optional AMR project or JSON paths from any working directory, with optional drawing suppression. The legacy editor entry point delegates to it. File New and Ctrl+N protect unsaved work, block switching during simulation/report execution and reset document selection, history and drawing commands. Fresh Save defaults to compressed AMR projects; imported JSON and recovered JSON retain their existing save behaviour. Save As uses the standard shortcut. Cancelled and failed saves preserve the current document.
limitations: This is a source/virtual-environment entry point, not the offline Windows installer. New projects are authoring drafts and still require valid layout, robots, demand and checks before simulation. Advanced CAD, run editing locks, broader traffic support and user acceptance remain open.

title: Approved A2 visual workbench in the production application
contract: Real workflow commands, File/Edit/View/Help menus, illustrated CAD tools, a narrow project tree, explicitly opened Properties side tab and current/stale/unchecked checks strip implement the approved graph-focused concept. Map themes include light, dark and high contrast with adaptive world-metre grid, measured scale, model-axis indicator, visible location outlines and compact optional legend. Personal fonts/colours and route patterns persist outside projects; legacy map preferences migrate explicitly without writing until Apply. Profile colours adapt for contrast at rendering while preserving saved styles. Clean/Dirty default colours are presentation only; access remains profile-defined. Door placement reuses nodes or splits corridors atomically while preserving profile/scenario references, width precision and undo. Fit includes visible outlines and proportional margins.
limitations: The visual workbench does not implement the entire CAD roadmap. Trim/fillet, full drawing layers, multi-object transforms and comprehensive geometry authoring remain open and are not exposed as inert controls. Door nodes are width restrictions, not invented wall openings or swing geometry. Dense labels still require zoom/filter controls. Existing playback retains its previous map rendering. Final human workflow acceptance and full tutorial remain open.

title: Graph-focused production workspace and CAD drawing interactions
contract: The compact toolbar shares existing edit, floor, snap and undo state. Properties and full tool tabs start collapsed; selecting objects does not open properties. Project tree and focus controls preserve panel state and unapplied drafts. Window selection encloses full rendered objects; crossing selection touches them, using viewport geometry with labels and underlays excluded. Shift/Ctrl toggles and Escape restores pre-gesture selection. Point hits use a six-pixel halo. Absolute X,Y, relative @dx,dy and polar @length<angle entries use metres and degrees, with finite numeric validation, visible object snaps and length/angle feedback. Typed input bypasses grid/decimal rounding; object snapping remains explicit. Drawing, splitting and property edits retain undo and portable project save/reopen behaviour. Drawing inputs are inactive outside Layout.
limitations: This is the first production CAD interaction checkpoint, not the full approved visual design or CAD roadmap. Endpoint and edge-projection snaps remain the existing fixed world tolerance; selectable snap types, orthogonal constraints, arcs/fillets, multi-object transforms, drawing layers, editing locks during runs and full keyboard/accessibility review remain open. Legacy advanced dialogs and dense labels still need rework; the A2 checkpoint separately delivers the visual shell and map themes. Panel state is retained within the running window, not across application restarts.

title: Explicit Simple and Detailed selection with frozen mode evidence
contract: Simple retains graph/capacity behaviour; Detailed explicitly selects geometric trajectories and keep-right traffic with finite movement inputs. Detailed requires explicit version-2 movement sets, separate wall/robot clearances, turning-reference metadata and initial placements. Selection previews structural changes and blocking readiness findings without fabricating physical values. Simulation and geometry edits share one undo transaction; cancelled and unchanged dialogs preserve input representation and dormant fields. Earlier geometric projects remain historical comparison mode. New managed manifests and event sidecars record the resolved mode, validate it against frozen inputs, and reject contradictory evidence. Older metadata derives mode only from its frozen inputs. Review displays saved mode independently of current editor settings. The independent twenty-metre case completes in 14s Simple and 16s Detailed with loaded acceleration/braking.
limitations: Detailed traffic and manoeuvring remain partial: geometric lifts/bays/people/scenarios/batching and general recovery/deadlock are still unavailable. Mode selection does not implement these missing interactions. Incomplete Detailed inputs can be saved for editing but are blocked from simulation. Complete numerical engineering input authoring and full roadmap release acceptance remain open.

title: Explicit reverse permissions and editable capability presets
contract: Movement schema 2 requires reverse permissions in both empty and loaded states. Legacy omitted permissions retain prior reverse-enabled behaviour through an explicit resolver and migration. Reverse permission is enforced before geometry, in timing and in recovery candidate filtering; forbidden directions do not consume search budget. Steering, pivoting and omnidirectional authoring presets change only pivot/lateral flags in the selected state, preserving numerical inputs and independently editable reverse permission. Standard robot edits preserve detailed movement/manoeuvring settings and extensions. Changed capability saves explicitly migrate permissions; cancellation and unchanged saves preserve the old representation. Enabling a capability without required engineering inputs fails without a partial save.
limitations: The capabilities panel edits existing valid detailed inputs; complete numerical authoring and Simple/Detailed migration remain open. Presets are permission templates, not verified vendor models. Reverse speed remains an explicit stored parameter even if reversing is disabled. General multipoint, omnidirectional and loaded/moving recovery searches remain open; capability permission does not prove geometric feasibility.

title: Configured turning-reference geometry and evidence
contract: Explicit millimetre offsets use forwards-positive and left-positive body coordinates. Configured travel speed, arc radius and translational distance refer to that point; body poses and loaded footprints remain centred. Forward/reverse support-line fillets preserve body-centre endpoints; pivot axis is explicitly body centre or reference point. Swept checks use the actual centre orbit, including translating reference-axis pivots. New schema-3 trajectories validate frames and replay without recomputation; zero offsets retain prior evidence and timing. Workbench controls support undo and project export; workbench and playback mark the configured point. Partial evidence separately reports reference translation and body travel. Body-stationary offset arcs require pivot permission, including generated lanes.
limitations: Additional connectors for some initial reference-axis heading corrections and displaced reversal supports are not searched; those requested routes fail explicitly. General multi-point manoeuvre search remains open. Distance means translation along the reference path, excluding angular pivot primitives; body travel is separately exposed. Production CAD properties and complete report metric labelling remain in later UI/report work. No automatic migration guesses offsets, timing reference or pivot axis.

title: Finite angular rates in curved travel
contract: Detailed circular travel respects configured rotation speed and angular acceleration/braking even when stationary pivoting is forbidden. Arc tangential limits also retain the linear, turn-speed and lateral-acceleration constraints. Circular curvature discontinuities stop translation before restarting, avoiding instantaneous yaw-rate changes. Equal signed-curvature subdivisions preserve timing. Actual durations drive energy, occupancy and saved playback; legacy saved profiles keep their recorded timing. Application input checks require explicit angular limits in both operating states.
limitations: This is stop-and-steer circular geometry, with no additional steering dwell. Steering actuator rate, jerk and continuous-curvature paths are not modelled. Explicit turning-reference transforms are covered by TURNING-REFERENCE-01; loaded footprints remain body-centred. Older geometric inputs without movement sets retain their previous constant-speed behaviour and do not claim this capability.

title: Atomic requester and parked-blocker admission
contract: One parked empty blocker and one requester can replace their old parked tails with complete coordinated plans. Conditional planning retains third-party occupancy and physical history. Admission checks both actual plans against the original ledger and commits both robots, payload/resource reservations and energy together. The requester uses its already committed plan for normal dispatch, and taskless retreat evidence is published only after acceptance. Rejection restores ledger identity, both robot states, resource claims and unpublished events/evidence, including streamed CSV output.
limitations: This is bounded single-requester/single-empty-blocker coordination, not general multi-robot negotiation. Moving or loaded blockers, multi-point search and proven deadlock detection remain open. Charging-dependent requester retries are not admitted through this recovery operation. Proposal-only occupancy views are not proof of safe execution.

title: Explicit geometric stops and partial-run review
contract: Exhausted bounded searches stop distinctly from unresolved blockage after all known events drain. Stable stop events bind reason, time and affected IDs to frozen inputs. Managed partial runs preserve full log verification and remain opt-in for review. Saved motion profiles reconstruct elapsed distance, pose and modelled traction energy; future bookings remain planned, and task outcomes require elapsed lifecycle events. Playback stops without accelerating clipped trajectories; investigation displays the reason and withholds full-run aggregates.
limitations: Blocked and search-limit stops do not prove deadlock. Runtime coordinated recovery and proven deadlock detection remain open. Partial stock/battery state and physical charging energy are not reconstructed; completed-run reports remain unavailable for partial runs. CSV time resolution is 1 ms; modelled energy is not measured physical consumption.

title: Verified taskless reverse and lateral yielding
contract: Parked empty blockers can follow verified forward, reverse or permitted lateral graph paths to a fitting marked place, or a safe graph anchor when places are absent. Candidates are ordered by verified route distance, must respect directed links, corridor cross-width, static space, full occupancy and energy reserve, and must enable an eligible waiting task before commitment. Busy/charging/held robots are not pre-empted. Recovery has its own journey identifiers, timings, energy and saved geometric playback without synthetic payload tasks. Reverse/lateral motion profiles and direction-change stops are shared by simulation, clearance, reservations and replay. Atomic joint occupancy APIs check all proposed plans together without phantom superseded tails.
limitations: Runtime recovery atomically admits one requester with one parked empty blocker; general multi-robot coordination, moving/loaded yielding, multi-point search, arbitrary off-graph passing-place connections and proven deadlock termination remain open. Candidate search uses existing shortest graph paths and a bounded candidate budget; failure is not proof of deadlock. Reverse/lateral recovery follows graph centrelines with full space reservation, rather than applying forward keep-right lane shifts. Explicit reference-point offsets are supported; general connector search and finite steering actuator transitions remain outstanding.

title: Complete-plan moving and stationary occupancy
contract: Keep-right traffic requires explicit nonoverlapping per-instance initial placements for multi-robot fleets; a single robot retains its physically checked charger default. Immutable time-indexed plans include initial waiting, recomputed moving swept cells, full loaded handling footprints, charging and indefinite final parking. Complete plans are checked before serial commitment, with reference-based rollback and no duplicated moving reservations. Saved initial positions and headings replay correctly. Structured candidate conflicts retain owners, intervals, sources and known releases; an unknown departure remains blocked rather than disappearing.
limitations: Atomic admission for one requester and one parked empty blocker is integrated; general multi-robot negotiation, moving/loaded recovery, geometric lifts/bays and proven deadlock termination remain open. Stationary blockers without a committed departure can conservatively prevent otherwise recoverable work. Search exhaustion now stops with verified partial-run evidence, separately from unresolved blockage and without claiming deadlock. Node protection covers conservative cores, not complete junction approaches; modelling physical boundaries is still required.

title: Separate wall and inter-robot clearances
contract: Explicit project wall_m and robot_m defaults accept per-robot overrides. Wall clearance expands static obstacle checks. Moving robot interactions enforce the larger total inter-robot gap rather than adding two full margins. Two-lane admission uses two loaded widths, two wall gaps and one robot gap. Legacy clearance_m remains an explicit adapter for old studies, not a universal engineering default. Invalid inputs reject consistently; saved inputs retain settings and edits stale checks.
limitations: Inter-robot enforcement now covers complete committed occupancy plans and validated initial fleet placements; yielding and geometric recovery remain open. Legacy studies retain their lane offset convention. Physical corridor boundaries still need explicit geometry.

title: Drawn stopping areas and protected doors/junctions
contract: Optional rectangular areas validate on import/run. Delayed geometric departures check the complete loaded footprint against walls, drawn no-queue areas and automatic door/junction core protection. Passing-place helpers choose the nearest fitting candidate by supplied verified route distance. Stationary claim helpers retain owner, continuous time and pairwise clearance metadata; no unknown departure time is fabricated.
limitations: Stationary plan ledger, initial placement and handling/charging/idle occupancy are integrated; parked-empty-robot graph retreat is integrated, while coordinated/loaded recovery and deadlock detection remain open. Automatic square protection covers node cores, not every curved approach. Passing-place reachability must be established by a route planner; helper success does not prove a retreat.

title: Acceleration/braking and empty/loaded motion settings
contract: Explicit per-type empty/loaded speed and acceleration/braking sets retime forward geometric paths, stationary pivots, task/charge timing, energy and saved playback. Forward/backward speed propagation preserves speed through constant-curvature primitives and stops at curvature changes, direction changes, pivots and endpoints. Arc speed obeys travel, turn, lateral-acceleration and angular-speed limits; arc acceleration/braking obey both linear and angular limits. Optional per-state minimum radius overrides the explicit existing manoeuvring radius. Saved profiles are validated; swept-time cells enclose actual accelerated progress.
limitations: Curvature changes use instantaneous rest without dwell; steering actuator rate, jerk and curvature-continuous motion are not modelled. Reverse and lateral geometric paths are integrated for taskless recovery; multi-point geometric search remains outstanding. Explicit reference transforms are covered by TURNING-REFERENCE-01. Old geometric inputs without movement sets retain constant-speed behaviour pending explicit migration; complete Detailed mode is not claimed.

title: Fixed numeric urgency for detailed dispatch
contract: Detailed moving-traffic dispatch selects feasible tasks by existing numeric priority, release and enqueue order, then the fastest eligible robot. Charging-only choices preserve the same task order. Infeasible higher-priority choices do not suppress feasible lower-priority work. Simple mode retains its comparison behavior; committed routes are not pre-empted.
limitations: Candidate limits still bound selection; batch geometric routing is unsupported. Complete yielding, occupancy-aware admission and deadlock recovery remain open. Available delivery continues to precede charging-only alternatives.

title: Keep-right trajectories and swept-time moving traffic
contract: Opt-in keep_right_v1 adds tangent lane transitions with explicit minimum radii. Loaded width plus clearance decides whether two lanes fit; explicit single_file sections retain their centre line. Short lane transitions fail explicitly. Conservative continuous footprint enclosures in 0.25-second cells reserve opposing, following and junction-crossing moving paths. Earliest admissible starts use bounded conflict searches; claims participate in transaction rollback and expiry. Saved traffic evidence identifies lane sections, policy and blockers, while playback uses the same recorded trajectory.
limitations: Moving traffic only: parked, handling and waiting footprints are not yet reserved and the application warns accordingly. Junction approaches return to centre-line tangent points. Safe throughput can be conservative by cell duration and swept enclosure size. Physical boundaries still require explicit obstacles. Lane transitions do not perform alternative path search; reversing, multi-point manoeuvres and deadlock diagnosis remain open. Documentation follows core and UI completion.

title: Geometric trajectories in simulation and saved playback
contract: Explicit geometric_v1 inputs use shared radius-constrained forward trajectories, permitted pivots, initial headings and continuous centred loaded-footprint clearance against modelled floor bounds and rectangular obstacles. Actual motion drives delivery, returns and charging time/energy. Transactional moving-route envelope claims serialize intersecting routes. Frozen project runs and saved playback use recorded curves and reject invalid evidence without straight-line substitution. A study exports to a separate runnable reference project. Legacy graph mode remains the default.
limitations: Conservative whole-route reservations are not directional lanes or parked/waiting-robot collision analysis. No reversing, multi-point or alternate geometric route search. Lifts, inventory bays, people, scenarios, multi-stop batching and inconsistent distance overrides block geometric mode explicitly. Graph widths/doors restrict access; physical walls and openings require modelled obstacles. Drawings remain underlays. Final CAD integration and user documentation follow core feature completion.

title: Explicit planar trajectories and drawable geometry workbench
contract: Analytic forward straights and minimum-radius fillets share motion geometry with rendering, exact distance/timing and continuous loaded-rectangle clearance checks. Explicit permitted pivots add rotation time. Requested-route infeasibility, collision, unresolved clearance and search limits remain distinct. A runnable graph-dominant prototype supports drawing, typed/snapped coordinates, draft cancellation, undo/redo, atomic study files, recomputed results and a worked reference tutorial.
limitations: Standalone planning study, not production simulation geometry. No traffic claims, lane/junction model, reversing, alternate path search, fixed endpoint headings, offset loads or simulator/energy/playback integration. Conservative unresolved bounds cannot establish passage. UI workflows await approval; the prototype PDF chapter is not the full application guide.

title: Consistent run-period defaults, preview horizon and settings preservation
contract: Import preserves direct-runtime omission defaults and release-spacing aliases. End date, duration hours, duration days and latest-static-release-plus-one-day fallback have consistent precedence in runtime and preview. End is inclusive generated demand, not a transport cutoff. Raw numeric/date/boolean checks reject malformed controls. Dialog saves only changed controls, retaining precision/metadata/omission and representing unlimited assignments and zero charging idle time. Legacy tick rate is explicitly labelled unused execution metadata.
limitations: No claim of complete scheduling heuristic, inventory bypass alias, charging or report verification. New-project explicit defaults remain distinct from omitted legacy defaults. Zero horizons retain start-instant runtime work; preview requires a positive duration. Runtime retention still protects twice the congestion window.

title: Legacy waste collection and initial-stock agreement
contract: Legacy seeds and collections agree on the global stream payload and department physical presence/group settings. Presence opt-out issues ordinary outbound stock; seeded cycles return the same ID. Extra independent/per-pickup shared bins and generation-disabled custom stock remain supported. Explicit named shared groups seed once, preferring the actual collection pickup. Modern-key/empty alias precedence applies to custom stock. Scalar and plural references rename/remove consistently; malformed names reject. Suffix assignment preserves existing references and matches exact/underscore extensions. Managed checks expose legacy-unused overrides and unsupported plural dropoffs.
limitations: Legacy collection uses singular routes and global container definitions; per-stream rate/type/capacity/enablement overrides remain modern-only. Legacy departmental volume pools do not merge when physical bins are shared. Custom seeding can remain enabled when legacy generation is off. Unknown custom locations are skipped rather than fabricated; broad custom/mixed-service stock, calendars and report reconciliation remain open.

title: Sparse department waste overrides and inheritance-safe editing
contract: Bare names canonicalize to name-only objects. Department, nested and bulk dialogs retain sparse overrides, payload/capacity/shared-ID aliases and extension metadata. Blank numeric controls remove overrides; explicit zero remains supplied. Mode Inherit removes the field, while Default (scheduled) retains explicit blank mode. Clear schedule is an empty override; Inherit removes it. Partially checked single-stream flags inherit. Bulk changes apply only edited fields; untouched departments retain their own settings. Stream assignment names must be nonblank strings and unique within a department after trimming. Generation fields use shared finite nonnegative scalar, boolean and mode checks; malformed values reject before returning an editor result/import/run. Existing time/calendar checks have their separately documented scope.
limitations: Reference tests establish sparse editing and specific scheduled/threshold outcomes, not all modes/calendars, physical stock cycles or report reconciliation. Bulk orphaned streams remain preserve/remove-only. Legacy pickup/seeding references and broad missing-reference checks remain under audit. Unknown extension fields are preserved without claiming execution support.

title: Shared provisional locations and stale department draft protection
contract: Deleting a department draft transfers its provisional point creation to one surviving effective user, preserving coordinates and creating the point once. Unused points disappear from choices and are not created. Shadowed aliases do not retain points; conflicting placements reject without losing drafts. Department child/list dialogs snapshot project ownership and configuration plus parent-list data, reject stale acceptance and retain draft input. Replacing the project store with identical data also invalidates the draft. Child seeds are independent copies. Existing accepted placement cancellation and one-step undo/redo remain covered.
limitations: Reference scope covers department dialogs and provisional point ownership, not all application modal workflows. Existing referenced-department deletion remains protected by the model. No automatic merge, unaccepted-modal recovery or persistent provisional canvas overlay is provided; final CAD workflow approval and broader release gates remain open.

title: Consistent department destinations and provisional placement
contract: Modern pickup_dropoff_locations wins over locations; dropoff_zone_locations wins over drop_off_zone_locations, including explicit empty lists. A category scalar/list is service shorthand. A scalar is one literal name, never comma-separated. Trim whitespace and deduplicate in first-seen order. A nonempty service assignment replaces category pickup or dropoff according to department_location_role; zones apply to delivery handoff with a service destination. Import canonicalizes effective selections without losing aliases or category metadata. Accept and deletion preserve explicit empty modern lists, so shadowed aliases cannot be revived. Unlisted categories survive editing. Placements remain provisional through child OK and are committed with department Save in one undoable change; cancellation leaves project data untouched. Invalid or conflicting pending locations reject atomically and remain available for correction. Known assignment fields must be a string or list of strings. Null, booleans, numeric names and object-valued names reject import/runtime/preflight. Effective missing location references block managed Project Checks; shadowed alias names are not effective references. Pending locations require unique nonblank names, finite nonboolean coordinates and whole floors.
limitations: Empty service lists retain category routing rather than disable demand. Unknown category assignments may remain unused. Raw simulation validates shape but managed Project Checks supplies missing-location preflight. Legacy waste_pickup_locations is retained without implicit migration to modern categories. Provisional locations are bare points requiring connectivity and capacity configuration; department stale-state and provisional-owner cases have separate acceptance evidence; full report/stock reconciliation and other modal workflows remain open.

title: Atomic department identities and demand-reference preservation
contract: Department ID edits replace the original record and remap group membership, override keys and static task department IDs atomically. Conflicting targets and referenced deletion reject without losing settings. List dialogs copy nested data and track successive ID changes; canvas edits undo/redo once. Duplicate identities/names, malformed identity/position values and duplicate group members reject. Incomplete identities remain editable but cannot run. Name fallback works in modern and legacy generation. Unresolved assignments surface no-work warnings. Department markers cannot hide graph points and moves retain precision.
limitations: Complete reference/deletion cleanup, external metadata and frozen runs are not remapped; category-location aliases now have a separate contract. Legacy label collisions are repairable drafts blocked by managed preflight. Provisional generated-location transactions now have separate acceptance evidence; stale department dialogs have separate acceptance evidence; other modal workflows remain open. General department/workspace and full demand/event reconciliation gates remain open.

title: Department openings and demographic waste input contracts
contract: Shared department intervals preserve overnight legacy-hour imports and nonmidnight full-day windows. Explicit end wins; equal clocks and zero legacy hours mean 24h. Subhour legacy waste uses the actual interval, removing the one-hour denominator clamp. Finite nonnegative demographics/coefficient inputs, boolean enablement, valid clock/day values and finite derived waste rates are checked before import/run and department upsert. Dialogs retain fractional values, legacy coefficients and unedited metadata, reject invalid input, and Project Checks explains the legacy-only demographic scope.
limitations: Empirical waste coefficients require external calibration; modern category rates and actual staffing capacity are separately configured. Identity/reference/floor/coordinate contracts, complete department editing and full mixed-mode/stock/event reconciliation remain open. Existing minute rounding and full-day equal-clock convention retained.

title: Nominal storage capacity agrees across report and simulation
contract: Reports count payload bays separately from AMR parking, honoring modern/legacy AMR markers and empty modern alias precedence. Shared dimension resolution covers modern/legacy units, zero inference, mixed local/absolute bay points at the location origin and payload size-unit defaults. Parent payload restrictions and flexible precedence agree with runtime. Report nominal capacity uses distinct compatible matching, including plan rotation, height and the existing payload tolerance. Missing geometry is labelled count-only in detail and summary output, never silently treated as dimensional proof. Runtime, editor, preflight and fleet checks resolve mixed bay coordinates consistently. Coordinate overflow rejects before import/run.
limitations: Configured capacity is nominal, not live availability. Does not reconstruct reservations or prove access, physical manoeuvres, actual assigned bays, queue behaviour or overall event coverage. Legacy/missing dimensions retain explicitly labelled count-only lower-bound shortfall comparisons. Drawn inventory area excludes AMR bay outlines and remains zero for dimension-only bays; it is not a polygon union or clearance measure. Full report reconciliation, absent-event versus zero-activity evidence and physical geometry remain open.

title: Location outline coordinates, measurements and model scope
contract: Complete local dx/dy pairs take precedence over legacy absolute x/y pairs per point. Mixed representations resolve consistently in editor metrics, report measurements and playback visibility. Editing preserves coordinate precision and point metadata; JSON and compressed projects round-trip, completed boundary edits undo/redo and cancellation preserves saved geometry. Translated shoelace arithmetic avoids catastrophic large-origin cancellation. Malformed containers, pairs, nonfinite/boolean coordinates and overflowing conversions or polygon metrics block import/preflight/runtime without mutating input. Nonempty outlines surface an explicit model-scope finding. The nine-second transport reference is unchanged by an outline.
limitations: Outlines guide drawing, storage arrangement and reported plan measurements, not simulation walls, containment or swept clearance. Arrangement uses axis-aligned envelopes and can exceed concave polygons. Short, repeated, collinear or self-intersecting outlines are retained; algebraic area is not proof of a valid physical room. Local points move with the origin; legacy absolute points remain fixed until explicitly edited into local form. Display/report rounding and binary floating-point precision remain. General storage-report reconciliation and future physical geometry remain open.

title: Direct scheduled and sporadic task-volume outcomes
contract: Dynamic scheduled waste and sporadic tasks, including hybrid discrete events, register each explicitly attached volume once. Requested volume equals pending plus completed-task plus failed-before-pickup plus unconfirmed-after-pickup volume. Return/duplicate callbacks cannot count fresh demand. New saved evidence contains component identity, coverage counts, grouped totals and per-task requests. Results Investigation checks generated rules/components/volumes, terminal outcomes, physical pickup evidence for failure phases, coverage of all tagged generated tasks, and exclusion from accumulated waste allocations. Known zero volume remains distinct from absent or old evidence.
limitations: These are recorded task outcomes, not independent reconstruction of configured demand or proof of physical disposal, decontamination or final staff handoff. Post-pickup failure is retained as unconfirmed task volume even if an intermediate physical arrival occurred. No automatic retry or stock restoration is inferred for direct events. Threshold pools, legacy waste, manual/timeframe tasks and tracked consumable quantities have separate scopes. Existing route-pair multiplicity applies; configured events and task records are not interchangeable.

title: Hybrid continuous and discrete demand without duplicate volume
contract: Hybrid uses continuous base volume for threshold collections and deterministic frequency events for separate direct tasks. Event volume is not also added to the threshold pool. Threshold and scheduled_threshold retain event-based filling; scheduled waste fills and frequency fills remain separate configured contributions in scheduled_threshold. Partial volume and closed-poll demand persist. One-hour references distinguish two legitimate components from the formerly duplicated third collection. Preview and four relevant editors explain mode semantics; category editors expose threshold event fields and plain scheduled waste disables unused frequency.
limitations: Hybrid totals remain runtime-dependent and no fixed hybrid preview total is claimed. Accumulated-waste balance covers its continuous threshold pool; direct sporadic and ordinary scheduled task volumes still require separate outcome accounting. Existing route-pair multiplicity and physical bin availability apply. This is a changed-result correction; historical runs retain their original frozen inputs and software identity.

title: Deterministic sporadic demand planning and retained events
contract: Sporadic and scheduled_sporadic modes accumulate deterministic fractional occurrences per 24 eligible hours, not random arrivals. Demand Preview shows poll-based releases and any clock-scheduled component in chronological order, with accrued/emitted/retained occurrence accounting and per-rule provenance. Missing valid route pairs retain whole events rather than discard them. Each emitted occurrence retains existing per-route-pair multiplicity. Inclusive final partial polls and the runtime minimum 60-second cadence apply. Independent Decimal arithmetic covers one route pair and unrestricted dates/hours; complex calendars use explicit hand-calculated references.
limitations: Preview does not dispatch, evaluate physical availability or simulate returns. Planned times precede configured runtime staggering. Additional tracked-stock demand and returns keep the overall total unknown. Hybrid/threshold modes remain runtime-dependent and their combined frequency/volume interactions need further audit. Preview bounds are 31 days, 20000 task records and 100000 sporadic poll evaluations. Retained events are generator state; they do not imply post-horizon retries or completed transport.

title: Legacy department waste outcome conservation
contract: Legacy accrued fill is allocated once to each collection. Failure before physical pickup restores fill once for a subsequent eligible poll; failure after pickup remains unconfirmed. Completion, failure and return callbacks cannot duplicate volume. Accrued equals residual plus pending plus completed plus unconfirmed. Restored attempts are diagnostic and not additional stock. Version 2 Results Investigation evidence includes explicitly identified dynamic and legacy generators, links legacy generation/outcome records and reconciles their allocations. Version 1 retains its dynamic-only scope.
limitations: Legacy per-department/stream rate and routing semantics are retained. This verifies modeled volume and task outcomes, not physical disposal or decontamination. A failure after pickup is not automatically retried because its physical arrival remains unknown. Restored fill is retried only on a later eligible generation poll within the demand horizon. Ordinary scheduled/sporadic demand remains outside accumulated-waste accounting. Broader mixed services, department stream override parity and inventory interactions remain open.

title: Tracked consumable stock and confirmed replenishment
contract: Continuous active-hour consumption is divided between department resources and retained across closing polls. Requests do not refill stock. Pending automatic requests suppress duplicates; scheduled top-ups deduct incoming supply. Confirmed completion/handoff credits ordered stock once, failure leaves stock depleted and permits retry. Top-up, full content exchange and replace-empty have distinct logical stock behavior. Initial plus delivered equals consumed plus removed plus remaining; unmet demand is recorded separately. Final balances, request states and confirmed delivery/handoff receipts are saved with coverage counts. Results Investigation reconciles per-item accounting against requests, terminal outcomes and matching physical arrivals; metrics link to contributing records. Old or partial receipt evidence remains unknown. Raw finite quantity contracts reject malformed input; ignored usage labels and mixed item routing are visible findings.
limitations: Stock is a per-rule/per-resource logical consumable balance, initially full, with unlimited supply at configured sources. Physical tote handling retains the existing exchange/handoff model; distinct handling workflows for each content mode are not established. Stock is credited at confirmed direct completion or at the existing staff-handoff commit, not backdated to its planned walking arrival. Consumption ends at the demand horizon while already requested supplies may arrive later. Mixed-source/mixed-payload requests and usage_rate-specific stochastic schedules are unsupported and warned. Cross-rule shared stock, partial deliveries, stock expiry and independent reconstruction of all consumption intervals remain open.

title: Accumulated waste allocation and outcome reconciliation
contract: Each pooled threshold funds one collection; alternative route pairs no longer multiply its volume. A pre-pickup failure restores its allocation exactly once for later retry. Completed collections, pending allocations, residual volume and post-pickup unconfirmed volume reconcile accrued demand. Return outcomes do not duplicate or restore collection volume. Recorded group and per-task allocation events with coverage counts drive Results Investigation metrics and event links. Totals and task outcomes are cross-checked; missing evidence stays unknown.
limitations: Balance covers dynamic accumulated volume and threshold collections, not ordinary scheduled/sporadic work, legacy waste, tracked-item consumption or physical disposal. Post-pickup failures remain unconfirmed; recovery-to-volume reconciliation is not implemented. Cancelled/partial/older logs have unknown full coverage. Candidate-route selection is deterministic round-robin per pool among the triggering rule's valid pairs; it does not model a spatial waste distribution within that pool.

title: Initial bins follow resolved active Waste rules
contract: Modern Waste seeding uses the existing generator resolver for effective pickup, payload, group identity and initial presence. Disabled department/stream/group contributors cannot choose stock. A globally disabled enabled-modern definition seeds no rule-owned bins. Active contributors alone participate in shared-definition conflicts. Automatic shared groups use the full pickup signature and seed one bin at the first viable configured pickup; full cycles preserve that ID. Unavailable seed space creates no replacement stock and waiting demand can expire. Department presence overrides category defaults. Legacy/custom seed behavior remains on an explicit adapter.
limitations: Active legacy services now resolve stock type and group with their collection tasks; custom services without active waste rules retain the raw seed adapter. Multiple independent department bins, orphaned references and all inventory priority combinations remain unaudited. Threshold failure restoration, multi-pair waste-volume accounting and tracked-item consumption remain open; physical bin conservation does not prove waste-volume conservation.

title: Shared physical bin identity, delayed return and definition checks
contract: Department payload overrides seed the correct bin. Grouped tasks cannot borrow another group at the same pickup. Forced same-instance returns retain delay and route profile even without a generic return payload, including tasks bound after the bin returns. Failed outbound travel retains the bin at source; failed return retains it at destination, and waiting demand expires without duplicating it. Active dynamic shared contributors must agree on resolved payload, capacity, threshold and initial-presence flag; structured checks and runtime reject disagreements. One-route scheduled references conserve physical identities through editor import.
limitations: Raw seed definitions still differ from resolved demand rules: category/group inheritance, inactive seed contributors, automatic multi-pickup grouping, limited inventory spaces and legacy lifecycle combinations remain unaudited. Threshold volume is consumed when collection is generated, not proof of completed transport; failure restoration and multi-pair volume conservation remain open. Forced seeded returns still inherit outbound profiles when their return profile is blank.

title: Waste threshold precedence and legacy conservation
contract: Dynamic derived thresholds use effective capacity and fraction after department stream overrides, while positive explicit thresholds win. Compatible shared contributors reconcile accrued volume to collected plus residual volume; separate bins stay separate. Legacy polls retain closed-time fill, decimal equality creates the correct number of collections, and invalid routes retain volume without incrementing task counts. Dynamic invalid routes also retain fill. Plain editor import preserves legacy enablement and priority without injecting an enabled modern Waste template. Shared flags and waste dimensions have raw checks.
limitations: Does not establish complete physical bin/return lifecycle, incompatible shared definitions or multi-pair collection semantics. Legacy demand-dialog migration and waste coefficients remain to be audited; global definitions still control legacy thresholds. Earlier provenance screenshot documents historical arithmetic and is superseded by the new review.

title: Calendar-aware accumulated demand and conservation
contract: Accumulation integrates category-active and department-open time across each polling interval. Polls at closing retain prior eligible demand; inactive weekdays and fortnight blocks add no volume. Pending threshold and sporadic work releases on a later eligible poll, including when no new demand accrued. Reference arithmetic conserves collected plus residual volume and fractional event counts. Numerical equality tolerances prevent missing decimal collections/events. Shared raw checks reject malformed rates; preview explains that continuous volume alone does not trigger collections.
limitations: Release times remain poll-dependent. Reference tests cover dynamic single-pair rules; shared waste pools, legacy generators, tracked-item consumption/resets and complete hybrid interactions remain open. A no-work preview is not a stock or physical payload-conservation proof.

title: Active-date allocation and explicit calendar exclusions
contract: Timeframe pool membership considers actual eligible dates throughout a window, including overnight weekday and fortnight transitions. Existing group ordinal semantics and release-date filtering remain; excluded slots are not redistributed. Independent references cover disjoint department calendars, closed members, partial horizons and raw/editor parity. Imported missing category/department weekdays retain unrestricted runtime behavior and dialogs display all seven days. Demand Preview records candidate-slot dispositions and reconciles eligible versus emitted records with explicit exclusions.
limitations: Slot accounting uses generator decisions and is not an independent expected-result calculation. Group ordinals do not book staff or optimise a shared calendar; differently sized department windows can overlap in release time. Accumulation-mode calendars, all malformed weekday inputs, global fixed-staff empty-day semantics and complete schema coverage remain open.

title: Overnight and disjoint working periods with visible fallback
contract: Timeframe release spreading uses the union of all applicable staff/department periods, including overnight carry-in, with no closed-gap or overlap double counting. Equal staff start/end means closed, consistent with runtime. Department group counts include overnight openings from a previous active day. No staff overlap preserves configured demand with explicit fallback reasons and preview counts; it does not authorise out-of-hours handling. Department opening at the exclusive deadline yields zero work with an explicit explanation. Rotating weekday restrictions are ignored consistently and reported as unsupported.
limitations: Spreading does not book staff or guarantee deadlines. Heterogeneous pooled calendars and category active-day/fortnight transitions remain to be accepted; runtime still has a flagged bounded-search fallback. Only the delivered reference scope is independently verified, not every calendar combination or all no-work modes.

title: Shared generation input validation and unsupported cycles
contract: Raw editor import, simulator construction and direct task-manager entry share checks for generation flags, mode names, selected counts/durations, staff patterns and custom hours. Malformed values fail with exact field paths before coercion; a rejected generation-settings edit leaves the store unchanged. Project checks expose custom work/rest cycles as unsupported warnings requiring acknowledgement, with dependency tracking invalidating old evidence after edits. Valid numeric strings, false/omission, zero polling intervals and named department waste-stream references retain compatibility.
limitations: Bounded validation rather than a complete schema. Unknown fields, all policy names, scheduling semantics, weekday lists and complete effective-rule interactions remain unaudited. Direct lower-level generator classes and static task metadata are not comprehensively validated. CLI constructors reject errors; unsupported warnings require the Project checks workflow for acknowledgement. Full feature inventory and application gate remain open.

title: Global staff switches and consistent timeframe releases
contract: Generation and runtime share effective staff-choice resolution, including legacy Stores labels, source, payload and generated IDs. Disabling global patterns gives generated tasks one all-day roster without disabling staff; custom weekly hours remain effective. The independent spread switch controls timeframe release distribution within global/custom hours. Fixed scheduled releases remain unchanged. Disabled patterns do not split otherwise shared custom-hour slots. Preview follows actual releases and no longer asserts an unspaced independent count for legacy staff demand.
limitations: Custom work/rest cycles, heterogeneous department-hour intersections within pooled timeframe groups, out-of-hours fallback policy and broad scalar validation remain open. Legacy direct/static task metadata is not rewritten. These checks do not establish optimal staffing or complete-run capacity.

title: Generated legacy staff tasks inherit working hours
contract: Generated tasks carry effective shift metadata independently of explicit or omitted staff choice. Runtime legacy Stores fallback now observes the same configured working periods as explicit true. False and non-Stores omission remain unstaffed; forced zone handoffs remain staffed. Independent raw/editor and full-simulation references reconcile staff finishes with return starts, including the existing saved return scenario.
limitations: Legacy direct tasks without shift metadata retain all-day availability. Custom work/rest cycles, mixed schedules and broad scalar validation remain open. Changed historical return timings require comparison with frozen earlier runs.

title: Staff travel and handling within alternating team blocks
contract: Valid four-day roster bookings constrain travel and handling to the selected team block, anchored to simulation start. A job that cannot fit moves to the incoming roster and recomputes its own travel and availability. Outgoing reservations and location history remain unchanged. Exact boundary finishes are permitted; overnight services cannot cross the team boundary. Incoming busy teams retain staffing expansion. An exhausted 35-day roster search retains the explicit working-hours fallback flag rather than looping indefinitely.
limitations: A flagged fallback is not verified capacity against working hours or team boundaries. Staffing remains conservative sizing, not capped queues or optimal rosters. Custom work/rest-day values are not used by the fixed four-day allocator. Heterogeneous patterns within one category and broader calendar interactions still need auditing.

title: Staff handling report reconciliation
contract: Reports include recorded handling and exchange events, preserve explicit Linen assignments and prefer logged initial roster counts and multipliers over configuration metadata. Task handling time is separate from the per-person union of recorded handling intervals. Missing person/interval evidence is unknown. Untracked department teams do not become invented headcount. New handling logs carry working-hours fallback and tracked-resource flags; legacy fallback status remains unavailable. Summary rows retain contributing event identifiers. Four-day team changes, return to team A, and work-period deferral across a team boundary have independent reference checks.
limitations: Recorded busy handling excludes travel and does not establish complete-run coverage or utilisation. Older timetables may still infer services from completion/return records and configured defaults; the new summary is not proof of their accuracy. Cross-boundary travel/overnight staffing, heterogeneous schedules in one pool, mixed tracked/untracked category rows and full metric navigation require further acceptance work.

title: Staff sizing and safe same-location batch bookings
contract: Independent reference bookings cover automatic pool expansion, shared overlapping services, travel waits, touching intervals, category pool identity, group override propagation, work-period deferral and explicit invalid-hours fallback. Stale batches cannot extend across a later booking; future batches do not delay earlier services; incoming work periods constrain shared finishes.
limitations: This is staffing sizing, not fixed-capacity queueing. No gap insertion or globally optimal staffing; nonchronological planning may overestimate headcount. Shared services retain historical per-task finishes, not one retroactively revised batch record. Full shift-team, lift-contention, busy-time and report reconciliation remain open.

title: Explicit staff choice and legacy omission
contract: Explicit false disables legacy Stores staff fallback; true enables it. Omission retains legacy fallback and survives editor roundtrips. Group false replaces category true. Actual staff records and completion-relative return delays reflect the effective choice. Physical zone handoffs still require staff.
limitations: Reference scope covers direct/static/generated choices and zone enforcement, not every staff scheduling/resource policy. Older normalised saved values cannot reveal whether a stored false was user-selected or inserted by an older version.

title: Generation precedence and imported return timing
contract: Category defaults are replaced by group/department fields; an empty group schedule suppresses category times and group membership suppresses standalone department work. Generated returns inherit the outbound profile only when the return-profile field is absent; explicit blank remains blank. Returns start after outbound arrival and configured delay, subject to staff handling. Imported rules no longer gain template staff flags or 15-minute handling when those fields are absent; new-project templates and explicit overrides remain.
limitations: Legacy Stores staff fallback, other omitted-template defaults, seeded/runtime waste returns and all generation modes still require broader auditing. Return counts are conditional and are not fixed demand-preview totals.

title: Routing flags and physical width input validation
contract: Project checks, editor loading and simulator construction share validation before normalisation. Routing flags require JSON booleans. Explicit widths must be finite and positive; all positive widths are preserved exactly, including below 0.1 m. Missing fields retain documented defaults; numeric width strings remain accepted.
limitations: This is a routing scalar boundary, not a complete configuration schema. Some interactive width controls still have a 0.1 m entry minimum. Old saved values already enlarged by previous versions cannot be reconstructed automatically.

title: Local route failure and endpoint preservation
contract: Valid local routes retain requested endpoints and clear expanded obstacle boxes. Invalid endpoints and exhausted bounded searches fail explicitly. Unsafe visual smoothing retains the clear polyline. Failed single and batch commitments restore resources.
limitations: Centreline and axis-aligned obstacle approximation only, not swept-footprint or radius validation. Unpositioned bays retain zero-movement behaviour. A bounded search failure does not prove global geometric infeasibility; alternative bay search is incomplete.

title: Application source binding for prepared runs
contract: Root and visualiser/report Python sources are fingerprinted. Changed, added or deleted sources invalidate prepared execution; historical results remain readable with an explicit older-scope warning.
limitations: Conservative application source binding, not a tamper-proof audit. Third-party packages and Python runtime are not part of this source fingerprint.

title: Routing and door defaults and option traceability
contract: Sixteen routing/door options have explicit runtime defaults, editor/import behaviour, precedence, validation boundaries, source symbols, support disposition and linked acceptance results. Directed/profile/width constraints compose; omitted auto-connect is retained on import and uses runtime true, whereas new editor projects explicitly store false.
limitations: Other option families still need individual audit. Seeded/runtime return interactions and UI width-entry consistency remain open. Passing linked cases does not promote partial behaviour to complete support.

title: Route-profile identification and access preview
contract: Layout and frozen-run playback share profile labels, contrast-checked colours, line patterns and direction arrows. Shared sections display every permitted profile; clean/dirty/shared remains defined by route profiles. The searchable table projects explicit and automatic same-floor graph access, combining node and directed-edge allowances with physical directions. Empty lists are unrestricted. Automatic reverse connections retain direction provenance. Lift allowances are listed separately and do not block same-floor transit at lift nodes. Malformed input disables the preview visibly; removed selections switch off. Styles persist per user by profile name without changing project/check/revision/run inputs. Playback uses frozen profile data. Independent directed reference cases, simulator agreement, styling/persistence, map interaction and large-text controls pass.
limitations: This is a permission projection, not a trajectory or feasibility assessment. Direct-travel fallback, task-local additions, combined loads, clearance, outages and timing are not displayed. Lift journeys are not same-floor corridors. Dense labels need zoom/filtering; automatic collision avoidance and standalone legacy viewer controls remain open. Schematic parallel strokes are not verified lanes or swept geometry.

title: Per-user accessible display preferences
contract: Project Appearance provides Light, Dark and High contrast presets, 8-24 pt interface text, 10-28 px layout text, custom text/accent/map colours and a visible or hidden map legend. Preferences persist separately from project/revision/run inputs. Existing standard controls are repolished and new controls inherit the palette/font. Active text is checked at 4.5:1 against preset backgrounds, accent at 3:1; selected text uses whichever of black/white has greater contrast. Invalid drafts do not apply, corrupt settings fall back visibly without overwriting, and failed saves retain active preferences. Apply does not alter project data, history or check currency. Pending property drafts survive. Reference contrast, persistence, live controls, keyboard actions and 1280x800 large-text behaviour are tested.
limitations: Playback map labels, timelines, drawings and some legacy custom controls retain existing rendering. Arbitrary underlays are outside contrast checks. Complete keyboard/screen-reader and dialog coverage, route-profile labels/patterns/colour preferences and accessibility compliance are not established.

title: Explicit recovery of staged containers
contract: A direct recovery task names an exact issued container staged at its pickup and marked as requiring recovery. It claims the container exclusively, applies ordinary robot, route-profile and destination-capacity checks, and moves it at scheduled pickup/dropoff. Rejection restores claims; failed recovery before pickup leaves staging intact, while failure after pickup records unconfirmed arrival. Confirmed arrival preserves physical identity/state and closes the outstanding recovery finding. Tasks UI exposes identity and recovery and preserves unrelated options.
limitations: Recovery is configured for a new run; it does not mutate frozen logs or resume a completed run. No unidentified or unconfirmed object is recovered. Staging geometry/capacity and direct recovery combined with staff handoffs or further automatic returns are unsupported. Existing manual-task robot compatibility rules apply.

title: Same-floor graph routing
contract: Euclidean edge lengths unless distance_m is supplied; directed edges remain directed; distance divided by constant speed gives travel time.
limitations: Reference cases do not prove all graph shapes or validate surveyed distances.

title: Door and corridor straight-passage width
contract: Passage requires max(robot width, oriented payload width) <= effective edge width, with 1e-9 m numerical tolerance. Effective width is the minimum of the corridor and its endpoint door openings. Select the shortest passable route.
limitations: No safety clearance, door height, opening time, door leaf swing or swept turning footprint is modelled. A door restricts both full incident edges.

title: Route profiles and task restrictions
contract: Route profiles define clean, dirty and shared access: shared sections belong to each applicable profile. Profile and task allow-lists are unioned; empty lists mean unrestricted; edge pairs are directed. The dirty task label selects the dirty profile only when no explicit profile is supplied. Unknown effective profiles reject scheduling instead of becoming unrestricted. Empty approach, charging and idle-return travel remain unrestricted by profiles. Returns use return_route_profile or their label fallback; seeded waste returns may inherit the outbound profile. Generating profile edges from selected nodes includes both directions of two-way corridors. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility.
limitations: No physical contamination-state model or empty-journey profile selector. Task allowances can widen a profile intentionally. Reference node, edge and lift intersections are verified; seeded-return and wider profile interactions remain incomplete. Static checks do not resolve every effective generation or runtime-return profile; the engine checks effective tasks before scheduling. Existing saved edge lists are not automatically changed; regenerate deliberately if reverse directions were omitted.

title: Corridor lane capacity
contract: Current two-way capacity approximation uses half corridor width and both loaded length and width to choose one or two concurrent lanes.
limitations: Not a directional keep-right lane model; no geometric junction conflict or overtaking verification. Length-based lane fitting is conservative.

title: Swept turns and multi-point manoeuvres
contract: Planned shared geometric model with explicit radius, pivot and reversing parameters.
limitations: Existing local manoeuvre drawing uses an approximate radius. Do not treat it as verified full-route swept geometry or steering dynamics.

title: Scheduled generation and override precedence
contract: Global disable wins. Enabled group/department rules can run under disabled category defaults. Group payload overrides category values and suppresses that department's standalone override. Separate groups are separate services. Category-wide zone capacity policy overrides ordinary group/department values; later department waste-stream settings are an existing exception. Category-only generation runs only without groups or department overrides. Polling includes the final partial interval at the inclusive demand horizon; released work can complete afterward. Clock schedules and timeframe slots now use exact calendar events. Effective pre-start releases are excluded; department opening adjustments can retain an occurrence across midnight. Consumption polling cadence is unchanged.
limitations: Exact release does not imply immediate assignment: resource waits, staff handoffs and configured staggering remain. Minute clock parsing is retained; fractional timeframe slots retain calculated precision. The wider generation-mode and calendar interaction matrix is still incomplete.

title: Consumption, threshold, waste and timeframe generation
contract: Generation derives demand from schedules, configured consumption and department assignments; tracked containers have separate balances.
limitations: Independent boundary cases remain for every mode, recurrence, waste volume, partial-day and timeframe allocation. Preview must distinguish runtime-dependent demand from fixed schedules.

title: Task assignment, priorities and deferral
contract: Deferral deadline starts at the original release and applies until assignment; zero means unlimited. Idle parking is excluded. One reference delivery takes 2 + 10/2 + 2 = 9 seconds.
limitations: Priority fairness, all candidate-limit interactions and end-of-run incomplete-task reconciliation need further reference cases.

title: Returns, staff handoffs and exchanges
contract: Returns and staff transfers retain physical payload identities. Same-container servicing records an arrival outside storage and returns the original bin; finite exchange stock is unaffected. Destination dwell and walking contribute separately to availability.
limitations: Existing regression coverage is broad, but a complete independent return/profile/staff-shift matrix is outstanding.

title: Location reservation capacity
contract: Reservations occupy half-open intervals. A request starts at the earliest time that existing simultaneous occupancy stays below capacity throughout its duration. Positive wash service now shares target location capacity with pickup/dropoff, records capacity waiting in route segments, and reserves only on a successful atomic route commit. Invalid service capacities reject before import/run. Independent 21-second uncongested and 27-second occupied-station references preserve physical delivery at 9 seconds.
limitations: These tests cover location reservations, not all lift, edge, staff or junction contention. Service occupancy is not physical queue space, and full local-manoeuvre interval alignment remains open. Washing is post-delivery robot unavailability, not a physical decontamination model. Loaded route profiles do not constrain the legacy unloaded wash transfer.

title: Inventory bays and payload instances
contract: Flexible bays accept matching dimensions with permitted plan rotation. Exchange deliveries and returns can represent different physical instances. Same-bin service arrivals do not create stored stock or consume a finite bay. Strict multi-stop deliveries require distinct compatible bays. Existing active claims cannot be overwritten. Temporarily full compatible bays wait until capacity is released or the original deferral deadline expires; without a deadline they can remain pending. Finite full-bin exchange plans claim distinct existing empty instances at commit, retain them in storage until outbound arrival, consume only their owned claim, and release unconsumed claims on rejection or task failure. Physical pickup/dropoff are scheduled independently of journey completion, including batch legs and post-delivery washing; completion fallbacks are idempotent. Equivalent-bin exchange requires an enabled return. Without it, deliveries need ordinary free storage and cannot consume empty stock. Tasks requiring existing source stock claim distinct physical instances at serial route commitment; estimates remain non-binding, rejected commits restore claims and task bindings, and pickup/failure releases owned claims. Exact and empty-only pickups take precedence over flexible selection; source pickups and empty exchanges cannot share an instance. Delivered stock can be collected again. An explicit ID on an ordinary outbound task creates at most one physical object: committed creation is exclusive, issued IDs require existing stock at the requested source, and in-transit or removed objects cannot be recreated. Creation claims roll back or release on failure before pickup. Generated IDs skip registered explicit IDs. Conflicting task payload types for one ID are preflight errors. Physical payload checks reject malformed dimensions, mass, preferences and duplicate/reserved identities before import or simulation. Runtime and editor share bay dimension inference: resolved template heights include legacy/default payload dimensions, modern fields precede aliases, flexibility aliases survive import, and inferred dimensions retain precision. Project Checks exposes unused payload and bay volume metadata. Shared bay checks reject malformed inputs and duplicate resolved names before coercion; unknown payload/AMR restrictions block running instead of silently broadening compatibility. The bay setter validates atomically, preserves dimension-only and legacy short-outline bays, retains precision/metadata, and uses shared envelope inference. Occupancy markers are explicitly distinguished from seeded physical stock in Project Checks. Shared AMR classification covers parent/slot markers and the legacy slot amr alias, including charger availability and editor compatibility. Parent and effective slot restrictions form the existing union; modern slot amr_type overrides the alias. Explicit AMR bays without charger flags cannot acquire a legacy location charger. Numeric and string zero bay dimensions share inference, and preflight accepts that convention while warning about unresolved plan extents, unbounded height and mixed definitions. Initial fleet matching maximises distinct compatible charger occupancy before extending with parking, preserving charger occupancy. Shared and instance-restricted bays count once globally. A breadth-first augmenting-path matcher is checked against exhaustive 3-by-3 compatibility graphs and charger/parking assignments. Project Checks reports scarce initial chargers as an acknowledgeable warning and unknown charging locations as blocking input errors. Legacy location-only starts remain explicit.
limitations: Reference cycles verify instance conservation and storage counts; system-wide conservation over long mixed workflows still needs independent evidence. Explicit staging geometry/capacity remains open. Direct staged recovery is verified in PAYLOAD-RECOVERY-01; unconfirmed locations cannot be recovered. Internal same-bin and staged-equivalent returns retain their existing continuation policies. Lifecycle counts distinguish planned, stored, in-transit, staged, unconfirmed and removed IDs. Physical population peaks include active issued objects; final identity records support state totals. Failed returns preserve staged identities and flag recovery needs. Staff-action timing and full mixed-workflow lifecycle coverage remain incomplete. Bay fit remains an axis-aligned envelope with plan rotation and 1e-6 metre tolerance; complete polygon geometry, live fleet rematching, charger throughput, complete location outlines and physical clearance remain under audit. Mixed AMR/payload definitions and legacy unbounded height remain explicit approximations with warnings.

title: AMR types, slots and multi-stop routing
contract: Robot and slot dimensions constrain payload compatibility; multi-stop tasks share movements. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility. Rejected serial multi-stop commits restore touched reservations, inventory claims, lift operational state, battery/energy and impact counters. Rejected individual and idle-return commits also restore task destinations, robot state and appended charging records. Shared raw/editor slot resolution preserves legacy dimension fallbacks and explicit slot precedence. Input checks reject malformed capacities, robot scalars, quantities, flags, duplicate identities/slot names and empty or unknown orientation permissions. Legacy comma-separated orientations resolve consistently for payload and slot. Exact capacity boundaries and permission intersections are independently tested. Project checks expose ignored per-type start locations and the robot-mass energy limitation.
limitations: Slot combinations, fleet contention, routing optimality and all orientation combinations need further cases. Greedy pickup-first stop ordering is not a complete tour search. Swept slot geometry is not verified. Distinct empty-bin claims are verified; atomicity beyond route planning remains a separate audit. Legacy size capacity is a per-dimension fallback, not volume. No independent aggregate structural payload mass limit or multi-slot geometric packing model is established. Physical payload scalar validation beyond orientation remains a separate audit.

title: Battery, charging and idle returns
contract: Opportunity charging is optional and admits idle robots progressively. Rejected charging-route plans retain departure occupancy and restore charger claims, lift operational state and robot targets. Estimates do not assign a target charger. One in-place charge reference verifies 10 kWh / 2 kW = 18000 seconds. Charger travel reserves corridor capacity, spends 75% of rated motor power over corridor movement, and recharges from arrival energy. Explicit waits consume no traction energy; lift energy is recorded separately and not deducted from the AMR battery on charger trips. Available battery may cross the reserve threshold but cannot be exceeded. The legacy recharge entry point uses charge-cycle events. Delivery and batch traction now uses corridor/local-manoeuvre durations and actual onboard load; explicit waits and lift travel consume no AMR traction. Lift supply includes boarding standby and is recorded once per journey. Exact committed traction must leave the battery reserve intact; estimates do not spend battery. At an operational charger, an individual delivery whose constructed route exceeds current battery but fits a full battery is retried after charging. The abandoned commit is rolled back, then routing and reservations are recomputed at the later time. Charging, pickup/dropoff and completion share one timeline. When no delivery is assignable, an eligible idle robot can request charging for route energy even above reserve. Each available compatible charger is checked for reachable arrival and a feasible full-battery onward task; commitment rechecks the selected destination. The original task stays pending and records route_charge_required evidence. Charger availability inspection is read-only; stale markers are cleaned only during serial claims. Investigation and report analysis share a source-attributed movement ledger: native event IDs count once, and complete bound logs with the energy capability distinguish known zero from missing evidence. Multi-stop task energy is unallocated; shared journey totals remain explicitly labelled. Transport groups containing shared journeys leave task energy blank.
