PDF lift totals use the same evidence and preserve unknowns. Planned recharge segments record input separately from applied battery credits. Complete bound logs reconcile each expected robot: initial plus applied charge minus traction equals final model energy, with separate counter checks. In-place charge credits occur at route commitment; separate cycles credit on completion. Missing or cancelled evidence remains unknown. Duplicate event IDs count once; conflicting duplicates are rejected. Explicit charger bays are reserved before travel and occupied at arrival. Separate charge-cycle IDs reject stale or duplicate events. Arrival and completion recheck charger validity and ownership; rejected cycles credit no energy. Busy chargers and failed charging attempts are operational events, not delivery task failures. Earlier delivery completions cannot clear a newer charging reservation. Identical local position and heading require zero movement. Initial fleet matching maximises distinct compatible charger occupancy before extending with parking, preserving charger occupancy. Shared and instance-restricted bays count once globally. A breadth-first augmenting-path matcher is checked against exhaustive 3-by-3 compatibility graphs and charger/parking assignments. Project Checks reports scarce initial chargers as an acknowledgeable warning and unknown charging locations as blocking input errors. Legacy location-only starts remain explicit.
limitations: Energy remains approximate: no stationary AMR auxiliary draw or robot own mass in the lift equation; rated-power/load formula is not a measured vehicle model. Fast assignment and pre-charge estimates omit some traffic and local-bay effects; exact individual-route shortfalls now replan in-place charging, and dispatch from non-chargers is covered by bounded references. Direct batch charging now replans the whole tour at the later departure, rolling back the original attempt. Charger detours check the entire onward batch and serial availability. Feasible deliveries precede detours; charged batches retain multi-stop preference among detours. Whole-fleet optimisation remains outstanding. Full-battery infeasibility is a route-attempt finding, not proof that every future route is impossible. One-bay/two-robot contention and fault-injected bay losses are verified. FIFO queues, idle-full-robot relocation, continuously monitored charger faults, partial charge after interruption, efficiency and wider threshold boundaries remain open. Locations without explicit bays retain legacy unbounded charging. Per-task batch energy allocation is deliberately unspecified; use movement events once for journey totals. Energy is route-plan consumption, not independently measured execution, and charging input is excluded from this movement ledger. Legacy logs lack corrected segment attribution. Atomicity after route planning and full report reconciliation remain separate audits.

title: Lift simulation and movement exports
contract: Lift transfers and empty repositioning are distinct movements; multiple tasks on one movement do not multiply its count. Reposition and loaded speeds are sampled at their planned start times. Committed routes remain fixed. Wear/failure-enabled lifts book in chronological commitment order; with both disabled, gaps are allowed only when the new recorded journey restores the next booking's original starting floor. No unrecorded reset movement is assumed. Committed journeys apply wear once; estimates do not. Rejected commits restore wear, repair and reservations. Deterministic failures use accumulated vertical operating time and a post-wear health-scaled threshold; boarding, doors and waits are excluded. Zero threshold disables failures; zero repair time still records a failure. Repair does not restore health; the minimum operating-health boundary is inclusive. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete. Shared scalar checks reject malformed lift timing, envelope, energy and reliability inputs before simulation. Floors/second is authoritative; lift displays show its physical equivalent and preflight warns about stale metres/second metadata. Editor saves avoid three-decimal floors/second rounding and omitted cabin/boarding defaults agree with runtime. Lift floor definitions are checked before import or execution: unique IDs, unique integer served floors, served start floor, exactly matching canonical floor-position keys, finite coordinates and noncolliding generated graph names. Missing fields can remain in editor drafts but block run checks. Rename collisions are rejected before callbacks mutate the project.
limitations: Commitment-order scheduling can leave gaps unused and can delay a robot behind an already booked later arrival. Dynamic replanning of committed journeys is not implemented. Mid-phase outage/speed integration, multiple-lift interactions, stochastic failures and complete report reconciliation remain unverified or unsupported. Health and repair state represent committed work rather than elapsed-time sensor state. Project Checks exposes these scheduling and reliability assumptions. Cabin fit uses max robot/payload dimensions rather than swept or stacked geometry. Legacy size-unit capacity has no fit/concurrency effect; no rated cabin mass or independent multi-robot co-occupancy is implemented. Valid rename/floor-removal reference migration and all editor range/precision round trips remain under audit; per-floor entrance positions need not align into a physical shaft.

title: People movement and congestion
contract: Configured people occupancy applies speed factors to corridor travel.
limitations: No dedicated independent reference suite for overlapping profiles, ramp shapes or time windows yet.

title: Scenarios and resource availability
contract: Scenario events modify selected resource availability and speed over configured periods. Scheduled boundaries wake pending work and invalidate estimates. Individual, batch and separate charging admission respect robot outages. Structural lift feasibility is independent of temporary availability. Windows are half-open and overnight weekdays belong to the start day; equal clocks mean all day. Original task deferral deadlines remain in force.
limitations: Already committed work is not interrupted. Mid-journey outages, chained corridor closures, lift repair/wear, speed-only interactions, DST and full malformed-input validation remain outstanding. Partial availability retains a speed-factor approximation, not stochastic uptime. Recovery boundaries are limited to the configured demand horizon.

title: Run period and simulation time
contract: Simulation times are elapsed seconds relative to the configured start datetime. Individual exports may round times.
limitations: Timezone/DST, all midnight boundaries and all end-of-run semantics need explicit policy and reference cases. tick_rate is not a physical accuracy setting.

title: Reports and metric reconciliation
contract: Tasks, AMR journeys, payload movements and lift trips are separate measures. Missing metadata must not be fabricated.
limitations: Complete metric-to-event traceability and reconciliation for every report measure remain outstanding.

title: PDF/DXF drawing import and export
contract: Drawings provide floor-scaled underlays; topology uses explicit world coordinates.
limitations: No automatic verified obstacle extraction from drawings. Broader import failure/scale coverage remains.

title: Editor validation and dialog behaviour
contract: Structured preflight reports severity, object, consequences and navigation. Exact known paths select common object/field properties, including parallel corridor records; stale indices and ambiguous point identities cannot select the wrong object. Per-finding input dependencies and evaluated/skipped check groups distinguish changed inputs from unchanged inputs. Returning through the workflow tree retains the old report until explicit recheck. All configuration changes still invalidate whole-run readiness and observed stale checks clear warning acknowledgements. Referenced drawing availability and project-folder changes invalidate live checks. Unknown and legacy checks retain conservative whole-project dependencies. Additive metadata preserves finding IDs and original schema-1 fields. Launcher snapshots checked inputs, findings, dependency evidence and warnings per run. Existing dialogs remain available. Shared compressed edit history supports undo/redo of completed configuration and canvas edits. Uncaught failures in an outer undoable edit or its history commit restore the previous model, selected identities and undo/redo branch. Nested edits roll back together; failed drag completion restores the pre-drag snapshot. Unchanged drawing caches survive rollback. A secondary refresh failure is attached to the original exception after model/history restoration.
limitations: Incremental checks, not a complete schema. Generation rule references need effective precedence resolution; legacy findings may lack exact navigation, and fields absent from contextual properties still require full editors. Drawing checks cover path availability, not content validity. File checks and storage remain synchronous. Undo groups existing dialogs and callbacks; individual command migration and systematic accessibility coverage remain outstanding. Transaction rollback covers editor configuration and history, not external file writes or arbitrary dialog side effects. Validation failures caught inside a command retain that command's own atomicity contract. Model-layer locking remains open.

title: Visualiser and task investigation
contract: Playback uses event records; failure navigation locates the affected destination.
limitations: Legacy playback remains supported. Results investigation adds evidence IDs and task timelines; shared swept trajectories and full report reconciliation remain outstanding.

title: Portable project, history and integrated application
contract: Compressed .amrproj stores deduplicated drawings and revisions with atomic saves and restore. Separate 30-second recovery copies preserve unsaved configurations and available drawings; Save/Discard/Cancel protects open/close. JSON export serves existing tools; results remain external. Project runs saves, checks and simulates a frozen saved revision in a separate process, with external results bound to project, revision and software identities. Optional versioned archive metadata persists external results roots and run references without embedding outputs or creating configuration revisions. Accepted new runs and relinks save atomically. Relative paths support moving a project/results bundle; Save As rebases links to existing folders. Missing references remain visible; relinking validates the selected run, revision/configuration and software identities. Metadata saves preserve unsaved configuration edits. Older archives without links open unchanged. A persistent workflow tree hosts Project, Layout, Configuration, Check, Simulate, Review and Report in one central workspace. Existing checks, demand, history, run and investigation panels are reused against shared state. Selected runs flow into investigation and reporting. Reports verify full bound logs and frozen inputs, run in a separate process, retain source/report software checksums, and remain external. Cancelled or failed reports cannot be opened as completed outputs. Review embeds revision-bound playback with a local timeline and monitors, read-only background loading, native event identities, independent reference positions, and stale-selection/project-switch guards. Playback pauses on leaving the workspace. Current edits cannot change frozen run inputs. Layout has a searchable object tree and contextual position, door, corridor and location-wash properties. Changed fields apply atomically with bulk previews and one-step undo; valid drafts are included in recovery. Stale drafts cannot overwrite newer edits. Robots, payloads, lifts, static tasks and route profiles have tree entries and common contextual fields. Route permissions use searchable node, directed-edge and lift selections, with explicit unrestricted-empty semantics. Untouched nested settings and identities are preserved. Lift speed edits synchronize floors/s with the legacy m/s representation. Managed simulation runs lock project editing, history changes, save/save-as, revision restore and run-link/results-root edits until completion, cancellation or failed startup. Shared command guards supplement disabled controls; native PDF drag paths are guarded. A persistent message explains the lock. View navigation, saved-run investigation and Stop remain available. Blocked property application retains its draft.
limitations: Playback drawing underlays, interruptible/paged large-log loading, nested configuration editing and object creation/deletion/renaming, broader identity/floor editing, removal/retention controls and large-project responsiveness remain outstanding. Configuration tools still use existing dialogs. Report generation is integrated, but PDF viewing uses the system viewer and complete metric reconciliation remains open. Storage/discovery operations are synchronous. Older builds may discard optional metadata; complete migration coverage remains open. The legacy launcher retains its machine-specific workspace path. The simulation editing lock is an application workflow rule, not filesystem locking or protection from external code mutating raw dictionaries.

title: Demand preview and rule provenance
contract: Frozen planned-task preview with filters, timetable, effective rule settings, no-work explanations and simple independent schedule reconciliation. Dynamic rules record ordered category, group, department and waste-stream assignments, including equal-value overrides, source paths and derived calculations. Effective settings exposes field histories; older and inactive rules do not invent sources. Runtime-dependent totals remain unknown.
limitations: Complex calendars, runtime inventory/returns, task-specific adjustments, global staff settings, inactive rules and implicit defaults still need complete attribution and independent verification. Waste threshold derivation now uses effective department overrides; department stream settings can still override category-wide policy after its restoration. Preview IDs are not simulation event IDs.

title: Results timelines and run evidence
contract: Recorded task outcomes and metric definitions link to contributing events. New logs retain stable event/journey identities, frozen inputs and source fingerprints; old logs expose missing evidence. Completed and failed task sets reconcile with bound run summaries. Payload service arrivals close transfers without adding inventory; logs declare this capability so older logs do not claim zero service activity. Failures after pickup and before dropoff record an unconfirmed physical arrival; no source stock or destination arrival is fabricated. Failed batch members cannot later complete. New full logs publish final lifecycle identities; investigation metrics link state and issued totals to those records. Missing lifecycle evidence remains unknown. Report task counts are independent of physical IDs; missing ID or physical-population evidence is not substituted with task or stored counts. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete. The investigation loader accepts files up to 300 MiB with a separate 250,000-event limit. Event tables display 500 records per page with previous/next and direct navigation; filtering and load failures clear stale event details. Pagination retains contributing records for review/export.
limitations: Planned segments do not prove execution. Payload pairing can be incomplete; wait causes are not additive; full PDF metric reconciliation remains open. Loading and analysis remain in memory; table pagination does not make parsing streaming or interruptible.

title: Corridor drawing, splitting and subdivision
contract: Explicit same-floor corridors can be split at a projected point or subdivided into 2-100 sections. Directed records share inserted nodes and retain attributes; distance overrides divide proportionally. Applicable route-profile, task, people and scenario references are rewritten atomically. Doors retain their identities and restrictions. Continuous drawing creates successive links with per-step undo and honors the bidirectional choice. Crossings remain unconnected by default. Explicit junction creation and intersection snapping join unique existing points, T-junctions and multi-way crossings. The default-off Connect crossings while drawing option previews all junction positions along a segment and applies the segment and all splits as one undoable edit. Any failed crossing leaves the original configuration unchanged. New branches are not implicitly granted restricted profile access.
limitations: Splitting changes the graph and can change reservation/people occupancy timing; identical congested outcomes are not promised. Auto-generated links must first be made explicit. Automatic crossing mode rejects collinear overlaps and ambiguous or near-coincident identities. Topological connectivity does not establish geometric or traffic feasibility. Curved edges, general trim/extend/offset operations and human workflow acceptance remain open. Historical links are not migrated for the former direction-checkbox defect.

title: CAD coordinates, snapping, selection and footprint authoring
contract: World coordinates and lengths use metres; angles use degrees counterclockwise from east. Corridor input accepts X,Y, @dx,dy and @length<angle. Grid snap defaults on at one metre, adjustable from 0.001 to 1000 metres. Object snap defaults to nearest points/edges within 0.45 m and offers graph endpoints, corridor midpoints, perpendicular feet from the route endpoint and explicit connected intersections. Exact coincidences retain topology even with attraction off. Mouse constraints offer free, orthogonal and 45/30/15-degree polar directions. Typed coordinates override grid/direction while retaining the selected object-snap policy. Previews describe the resolved point. Window/crossing and additive selection support shared-offset group dragging, numerical displacement, cancellation and atomic undo. Delete is available on the canvas via keyboard and context menu. Location rectangles support two corners or exact width,height[,angle] centred on the location; their coordinates are stored relative to the location. Undo retains unchanged drawing caches. Polygon drafts share mouse and exact absolute/relative/polar entry, last-point removal, Escape cancellation and stale-location rejection. Selection rotation uses an explicit centre and counterclockwise degrees with a dashed preview matching the committed coordinates; it rotates attached local/absolute boundaries, bay outlines and slot headings, preserves references and resolved bay dimensions, and commits in one undo step. Copy duplicates active-floor locations and corridor nodes, induced explicit edges, owned geometry and named-profile allowances with unique identities, a dashed preview and atomic undo. Internal wash targets remap; bays are empty unless occupied-state copying is chosen. Independent copied clean/dirty path distances remain 10/14 metres.
limitations: Object attraction tolerance remains fixed in world units. These drawing choices are session controls, not frozen simulation options. General trim/extend/offset, arcs/fillets, derived routes from drawn boundaries, comprehensive keyboard/custom-renderer accessibility and human acceptance remain open. Rectangle rotation authors a footprint; it does not validate swept robot clearance. Rotation operates on active-floor selected points and selected-edge endpoints. Connected edges to unselected points can change length; explicit distance overrides remain. Separate floor geometry and initial robot headings stay fixed and require project checks. Inferred bay envelope dimensions become explicit to preserve capacity. Mouse rotation supports centre/reference/target clicks with grid and visible-point snaps, coalesced ghost previews, cancellation and one undo. Transform reference picking now supports all selected object-snap modes without changing topology; perpendicular uses the base point or rotation centre. Hidden lines are excluded, and snap resolution is coalesced with previews. Polar constraints and physical clearance validation remain open. Copy requires explicit corridors and excludes department/lift duplication. External connections, operational demand/people/scenario rules, initial fleet and floor geometry are not duplicated. Move and Copy also support base/destination canvas picks, grid/visible-point snaps, coalesced ghost previews and one-step undo. Clipboard operations remain open.

title: Graph-focused view controls and selection navigation
contract: The graph-focused workspace uses a compact toolbar and collapsible supporting panels. Properties open explicitly; Focus canvas hides and restores supporting panels. Shared themes and map text size control presentation. Object-name filters offer all, key locations/departments/lifts/doors, selected objects, or hidden names without removing graph symbols. Filtered modes identify selected corridor endpoints. Profile labels remain separately controlled. Zoom to selection fits active-floor points, corridor endpoints and location outlines with at least one metre or eight percent margin, excluding underlays and without rebuilding drawings. These view changes leave model inputs and undo history unchanged and remain usable during simulation locks. Project-tree, layout/configuration property-panel and full-tool visibility, plus object-name visibility/mode, persist in versioned per-user settings. Layout and Configuration splitter proportions and property widths persist independently. Earlier records without sizes retain default sizing; invalid sizes are rejected. Focus canvas is temporary and cannot replace saved panel proportions. Invalid saved preferences retain defaults and are not overwritten until a view preference changes. Save failures retain session usability and expose a warning. Imported DXF layer names are retained for supported entities, including layer-zero block inheritance. A searchable optional dock provides visibility, show/hide-all and isolate controls with per-path user persistence. Toggling reuses batched graphics without changing model/history/camera state. Focus canvas and non-Layout stages hide and restore the dock while respecting explicit closure.
limitations: Model layers and editing locks are covered separately by MODEL-LAYERS-01. Line styling, persisted window geometry, collision-aware label placement, exhaustive accessibility and human workflow acceptance remain open. Offscreen regression cases do not establish the representative operating-workload benchmark or interactive LTN performance. DXF visibility retains the existing all-visible import default; source off/frozen flags and unsupported entity/block types are not newly interpreted. Drawing paths scope personal visibility; moved files have fresh defaults. Drawing layers do not become simulation walls.
